note_claims.claim: Head injury after a mechanical fall at home at about 07:45.
Tripped on a rug and struck the left side of her head on a door frame.
Patient reports feeling muddled for about 10 minutes afterwards.
Loss of consciousness uncertain (unwitnessed).
No vomiting.
Mild headache at the impact site.
No visual disturbance, limb weakness or neck pain.
No preceding dizziness or presyncope.
Last apixaban dose this morning, after the fall.
Tetanus up to date.
Apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily (atrial fibrillation).
Bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily.
Amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
Allergic to penicillamine (swelling).
Glasgow Coma Score is 15.
3 cm laceration with haematoma over the left temple.
Pupils are equal and reactive.
Normal power in all limbs.
No cervical spine midline tenderness.
Heart rate is irregular at about 80, and blood pressure is 146 over 82.
CT head (anticoagulated) is required to ensure no bleeding inside.
Wound cleaned and closed with steri-strips.
If CT normal, discharge with daughter, who will stay with her for 24 hours.
Call 999 or return immediately if she becomes drowsy, confused, vomits again, has a worsening headache, a fit, or any weakness.
Written head injury advice given to daughter.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician is Dr Pemberton and is speaking to Mrs Castellan.
Relative identifies herself as her daughter, Sue.
Clinician asks Mrs Castellan what happened.
Patient reports tripping on a rug in the hall and banging her head on the door frame.
Clinician asks what time the fall occurred.
Patient initially states the time was about half past nine.
Relative corrects the time, stating it was about quarter to eight, noting the post hadn't come and breakfast hadn't been eaten.
Patient acknowledges the correction.
Clinician asks which side of the head was hit.
Patient states she hit the left side, by her eye.
Clinician asks if the patient blacked out.
Patient states she doesn't think she blacked out.
Relative states that when she arrived ten minutes later, the patient was muddled and kept asking what day it was for about ten minutes.
Clinician asks if the patient remembers the relative's observation.
Patient states she does not remember Sue arriving.
Clinician asks if the patient has been sick.
Relative states the patient was sick once in the car on the way to the clinic.
Patient denies being sick.
Clinician asks if there is any headache now.
Patient reports a bit of a headache where she hit it.
Clinician asks about vision problems or weakness in arms or legs.
Patient states she has no problems with vision, arms, or legs.
Clinician asks about neck pain.
Patient states her neck is fine.
Clinician asks if the patient felt dizzy or faint before the fall.
Patient states she did not feel dizzy and caught her foot on the rug.
Clinician asks what medicines the patient is on.
Relative lists the medications: Apixaban 2.5 mg twice a day (for heart rhythm), Bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily, and Amlodipine 5 mg.
Clinician asks when the patient last took the apixaban.
Patient states she took the apixaban this morning with her breakfast, after the fall.
Clinician asks about allergies.
Patient states she is allergic to penicillin, which causes swelling.
Clinician performs examination: GCS is 15. There is a 3 cm laceration with a bump around it on the left temple. Pupils are equal and reactive. Strength is normal everywhere.
Patient acknowledges the examination findings.
Clinician presses on the back of the neck and asks about pain.
Patient states there is no pain.
Clinician notes the patient's heart rate is irregular at about 80 and blood pressure is 146 over 82.
Relative asks what happens next.
Clinician plans a CT scan of the head because the patient is on a blood thinner and needs to check for internal bleeding.
Relative acknowledges the plan.
Clinician plans to hold off the evening dose of apixaban until the scan is reviewed.
Patient agrees to the plan.
Clinician plans to clean and close the cut with steri-strips and asks about tetanus status.
Patient confirms she is up to date with tetanus.
Clinician plans discharge with the daughter staying with her for 24 hours if the scan is normal.
Relative agrees to stay with the patient.
Clinician provides safety-netting instructions: call 999 or return immediately if the patient becomes drowsy, confused, vomits again, has a worsening headache, a fit, or any weakness.
Relative confirms she will follow the safety instructions.
